Comment: A trial of the Quake example at Wikipedia scale on the lab server, before the cluster runs: the first two minor batches of the 2026-02 diff (b4x5: 775K inserts and about 744K deletes each), each followed by a round of Quake's maintenance as a major epoch (internal/update/quake.go: its cost model on the hits of the entries' last 10,000 client queries decides which lists to delete and split; the splits' neighbourhoods are refined, empty lists removed), on Quake's index: a flat k-means of round(sqrt(N)) = 3,939 lists, one replica a vector (fusion_build --from-index the base index --clustering kmeans; the base's IDs, raw-vector locations, codebook and page file), inserts routed to their nearest head. Quake's parameters are its Wikipedia configuration's (Quake's repository, test/experiments/osdi2025/wiki_workload/configs/wiki.yaml, the configurations with maintenance: window_size 10000, refinement_radius 50, split_threshold_ns 250, delete_threshold_ns 500000, enable_delete_rejection false), the rest its defaults; its nc 1000 is not taken: the paper sizes its indexes at sqrt(|X0|). QuerySample 2500: the 4 entries keep the window's 10,000 queries. The partitions are GP-64 with each head weighing its list's postings (Weights postings). NProbe, with --max-nprobe the same, is the smallest that reaches the base index's recall at nprobe 64, N 200 (0.8891; results/kmeans-index-2026-11-26/summary.txt): 96 (recall 0.9108), set by trial.sh. It checks that the rounds run at this scale and measures them (updates.json: quake), so that the cluster runs can be set; its timings are the lab's. CPU backend (the GPUs are other users'), 8 CPUs and 24 GB a node, no read limit, 100 q/s (at nprobe 96 the CPU nodes queued at 200 q/s in the first trial). No warmup snapshot: the nodes bootstrap from the page file, into a work directory on /netsys (copies of the assignment and partitions, with their stage records), which has room for their raw files. GraphHeadroom 6: Quake's first round on this index splits about half its lists (1,994 of 3,939 in the lab server's first trial, which stopped at the default room of 0.2: its cost model, on our scan profile, wants lists several times shorter than sqrt(N)'s), and a deleted head keeps its place in the graph.
